name: Nethaniah
overview: Nethaniah was a male Levite known for being sent by King Jehoshaphat as part of a delegation, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:8. His role reflects the responsibilities entrusted to the tribe of Levi in service to God's people during this period. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethaniah means "y-h-v-h has given," highlighting a recognition of God's providence. This proper name reflects a common theophoric element in Hebrew names, emphasizing the Lord's active role in granting life or blessing. The name itself does not indicate a title or unique office beyond his Levitical identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Nethaniah as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the priestly tribe responsible for temple duties. No further family relationships or surnames are recorded beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Nethaniah's significance lies in his service as a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat, illustrating the king's reliance on the Levites to teach and uphold the law among the people. His mention in 2 Chronicles 17:8 underscores the importance of faithful ministry and instruction in the covenant community. Through his role, Nethaniah contributes to the biblical emphasis on obedience to God's statutes and the spiritual leadership provided by the Levites.
